chunks: As for what Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Abū ʿAbdillah, from his father, peace be upon them:

“He would fumigate the deceased with al-ʿūd in the censer, and that is musk; and sometimes he would place the ḥanūt upon the bier, and sometimes he would not place it; and he used to dislike that the deceased be followed with the censer.”
So this is to be understood as a form of taqiyyah, because it is the doctrine of many of the ʿāmmah, and what we have mentioned is further clarified by what follows.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection in a context of opposing public practice
key_terms.النَّعْشِ: the bier on which the deceased is carried
key_terms.الْحَنُوطَ: the funerary perfume or substance applied to the deceased
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the broader non-Shiʿi public or majority
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person being prepared for burial
key_terms.الْمِجْمَرَةِ: the censer used for burning incense
key_terms.الْمِسْكُ: musk used as a fragrant substance

ai.seo_question: How is a hadith about fumigating the deceased in Tahdhib al-Ahkam interpreted through taqiyyah?
ai.summary: This passage cites a report about fumigating the deceased and placing ḥanūt on the bier, then explains that the report is to be interpreted as having been issued under taqiyyah. Its significance is juristic, showing how a hadith may be contextualized when its apparent ruling accords with the position of many among the ʿāmmah.
